name: Magahi
notes: Magahi (मगही), an Eastern Indo-Aryan (Bihari) language of Bihar and Jharkhand, India, ~13 million speakers, written in DEVANAGARI — an ABUGIDA: each consonant letter carries an inherent vowel /ə/ which is cancelled by virama and overridden by vowel matras, and the mapping must also handle schwa deletion. GRAPHEMES: the Devanagari letter-to-sound conventions (which vowel matra reads to which quality, virama behaviour, nasalisation marks) are the SAME reading convention Hindi's spec already encodes (`graphemes_base: hi`), following the precedent set by `doi` (Dogri) in this dataset: this is a claim about how the shared script is read, independent of each language's own phonology, which is instead declared directly in `phonemes` below (Grierson 1903). INPUT CONTRACT: Devanagari Magahi text (Unicode, NFC). KNOWN GAP: Magahi has phonemes (e.g. /ə̃ĩ/, /ə̃ũ/, aspirated /lʰ/, /rʰ/, /mʰ/, /nʰ/) that Standard Hindi's own inventory does not distinguish the same way; the inherited grapheme table does not yet carry Magahi-specific overrides for these, a gap left honest rather than guessed. STRESS: Grierson (1903) and the descriptive literature on Magahi report no lexical stress contrasts; left unencoded here, a documented exemption. TIER: no WikiPron (or other registrable) gold exists for `mag` (checked against CUNY-CL/wikipron's scrape summary, 2026-08-03: zero rows), so `skeleton`, not `research`.
